explanation: Allocate a result sequence and place original A[i] directly at result[perm[i]]. A separate result prevents writes from destroying values still needed.
timeComplexity: O(n+1): allocate n slots and perform one indexed assignment per entry.
spaceComplexity: O(n+1) returned storage and O(1) other state.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: Each original index i writes its value to the required destination perm[i]. Because perm is a bijection of 0..n−1, every destination is written exactly once. Reading only the unchanged input ensures each write uses the original value, proving the specified movement.
walkthrough: For perm=[2,0,1] and A=[10,20,30], write 10 to result[2], 20 to result[0] and 30 to result[1]. Return [20,30,10].
edgeCases: perm contains each index 0..n−1 exactly once and has the same length as A.
Empty inputs and fixed points need no moves.
The direction is original i → perm[i], not new A[i]=old A[perm[i]].
Equal values still move according to their original positions.
